2. Shri Akhilesh Singh, learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant sustained 70%
disability on account of amputation of his right leg below thigh, but learned Tribunal has awarded arbitrary compensation without taking into consideration the law on the subject.

3. Shri V.K. Trivedi, learned counsel for the respondent No.3-insurance company, in his turn,
supports the impugned award and submits that no indulgence is called for in the same.

4. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, it is evident that learned Tribunal has considered income of the claimant at Rs.2,500/- per month or Rs.30,000/-
per annum, which is not disputed, 70% of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:11804 2 MA-3858-2007 which will come out to Rs.21,000/- per annum.
Age of the claimant has come on record to be 40 years and, therefore, learned Tribunal has applied multiplier of 15.

Looking to the age of the claimant, 40% is to be added towards future the prospects and then multiplier of 15 is to be applied, which when applied will come out to Rs.4,41,000/- in place of Rs.3,00,000/- awarded by the learned Tribunal.

Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.1,41,000/- under the Shishupal Singh vs Dinesh Kumar Duvedi on 10 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198261848/

sentences.text: Tribunal has only awarded a sum of Rs.25,000/- under the head of Artificial limb, which is enhancement to Rs.1,00,000/-.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.75,000/- under the head of Artificial Limb.
Learned Tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of loss of amenities for which a sum of Rs.50,000/- is awarded.
Beside this, learned Tribunal has awarded a meager amount of Rs.5,000/- under the head of Pain & Suffering which is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.45,000/- under the head of Pain & Suffering.

5. Thus, there will be enhancement to the tune of Rs.3,11,000/- (Rupees Three Lac and Eleven Thousand only) to which claimant will be entitled to in addition to the amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal.
This additional amount will also earn interest at the rate of 7% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of actual payment.
Other terms and conditions of the award shall remain intact.
6. In above terms, these miscellaneous appeal is disposed of.
7. Record of the learned Claims Tribunal be sent back.
